newsitem.title: FRANCE: French truck blockade reaches refinery near Paris.
newsitem.headline: French truck blockade reaches refinery near Paris.

text.p: Oil disruption crept closer to the French capital on Monday as truckers blockaded Elf Aquitaine's Grandpuits refinery near Paris, industry officials said.
More than half of France's 13 refineries were now blocked as truckers tightened a stranglehold around major oil installations to reinforce an eight-day-old haulage strike, they said.
"The majority of refineries are blocked or have an uncertain situation. There are four we know about which are not blocked," a spokeswoman for oil industry association UFIP said.
Those free from disruption included Elf's Feyzin plant which serves France's second city Lyon, she said.
Deliveries from the plant had been disrupted last week.
The UFIP spokeswoman said Grandpuits, a relatively small refinery, had been blocked on Monday morning.
An Elf spokesman said it was the refinery's fuel depot for road tankers which was surrounded.
UFIP said most of the strategic depots which link refineries and retail petrol stations in France were now inaccessible.
France has 175 such storage sites, most of them owned wholly or in partnership agreements by the major oil firms.
Of France's 18,000 stations, only a hundred or so have run out of petrol, industry officials said.
But many of these were concentrated in a handful of towns like Bordeaux, Marseilles and Caen, making life difficult for motorists who had to queue at supermarkets for scarce petrol.
Refineries depend on road tankers for around a third of their deliveries, including most fuels used for transport.
Supplies of unleaded petrol were worst hit as motorists filled their tanks, industry sources said. There was no problem with diesel fuel, partly because lorries were standing still.
Life in the capital was normal with no signs of shortage at filling stations.
But oil industry officials warned of widespread possible disruption if the strike continued more than a few days.
"If the blockades last another 48 hours we will have a much more difficult situation," a spokesman for France's second largest oil company Total, said earlier.
Truckers' unions have said their strategy is to block vital access points for fuel outside the capital while keeping direct action against Paris in reserve.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe urged truckers and haulage bosses to reach a deal after all-night talks with a state-appointed mediator failed to break the deadlock over pay and working time.
